title: Delete Confirmation Connector and Proof API
creator: Lena Patel
description: Problem statement: Customers operating under regional privacy regimes want a guaranteed, auditable flow for Right-To-Be-Forgotten requests that: (1) confirms ingestion of the erase request synchronously to the caller, (2) provides machine-verifiable proof that data was expunged (or scheduled for deletion) across all residency zones, and (3) surfaces a reconciled timeline when eventual-consistency background jobs may delay physical expunge. Goals: - Provide a public Delete Confirmation Connector API that returns a signed acknowledgement and a short-lived proof token at request time. - Implement a Proof API / verifier that customers can poll or call to obtain an attested deletion status, per-region tombstone hashes, and reconciliation notes if background jobs are still in-flight. - Integrate with retention-policy simulator so admins can preview whether an item is deletable immediately or will be deferred by policy (and why). - Add console UI that shows per-tenant deletion pipeline state, region-by-region progress, and evidence export in ZIP/JSONL with signed manifests. Success metrics: - 90% of RTBF requests receive an acknowledgement within 300ms. - 95% of proofs reflect final state within SLA window (72h for cross-region, 6h for single-region). - Support exportable evidence bundles compatible with auditors (checksumed, timestamped, signed). Non-goals: cryptographic notarization by third-party (out of scope for MVP), large-scale bulk erasure tooling (later phase).
acceptance_criteria: API: DELETE /v1/tenants/{t}/data/{id} returns 202/200 with signed acknowledgement payload and proof_token when request is accepted
Proof API: GET /v1/tenants/{t}/proofs/{proof_token} returns current_status, per-region hashes, last_updated, and signed attestation
Simulator: console + API endpoint that evaluates retention rules and returns decision and explanation for any given record id
Evidence export: Administrator can generate zip containing JSONL of events, per-region tombstones, SHA256 checksums, and a signed manifest
Console: tenant-level timeline visualizer showing enqueue -> expunge steps and links to evidence exports
Security: proofs and manifests are signed with KMS-managed keys; RBAC restricts export endpoints to admin roles
Observability: trace id propagated across the orchestration; cost/latency metrics emitted to console dashboards
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (alpha): internal-only toggle enabled for Compliance team; run against isolated dev tenants
Phase 1 (beta): invite customers enabling 'auditable-rtbf' feature flag; collect feedback and edge-cases
Phase 2 (general): enable by default for Dedicated and Hosted customers behind retention controls; add docs
Fallback: automatic revert to non-attested deletion with an advisory when KMS signing fails; alert on security channel
implementation_notes: Design: use existing event-sourcing stream for deletion workflow; append tombstone events with region tag
Proof token: short opaque token referencing canonical deletion_request_id; token contains request timestamp and signed HMAC to prevent tampering
Reconciliation: run probabilistic reconciler that compares tombstone registry with storage layer indexes and surfaces diffs
Retention simulator: reuse rules engine from billing-pipeline with additional explainability output
Visibility: new route-level telemetry to measure synchronous ack latencies separately from background expunge delays
Export format: JSONL events + manifest.json with sha256 checksums, base64-encoded KMS signature and UTC timestamps
open_risks: KMS signing throughput may bottleneck large export requests -> consider batched signing or ephemeral signing keys
Cross-region deletion semantics differ by cloud provider; need legal review for per-region latency SLAs
Customers may expect immediate permanent deletion; must clearly label 'logical deletion' vs 'physical expunge' in UX
Replay/idempotency for delete requests must be robust to avoid double-expunge or missed evidence
qa_plan: Unit tests for proof token generation and KMS signing logic
Integration test: end-to-end delete request -> proof token -> final proof matches exported manifest
Chaos test: region outage simulation to verify reconciliation notes and eventual consistency behavior
Performance test: run synthetic workload to ensure 300ms ack for 90% of requests under normal load
Pen test / threat model on proof endpoints and export ZIP handling
